question: The EU has adopted a reinforced strategy to combat forest fires. This led to a doubling of resources in 2023. This strategy is part of the EU Civil Protection Mechanism (EUCPM) which can be activated by a state that does not have sufficient resources to cope when a disaster strikes, such as a forest fire, a flood or an earthquake.

Climate change, which is affecting the whole world, as well as the forest fires that are now spreading to overseas territories (as was the case last year in New Caledonia, near Poum) are justifiable reasons for the EU to expand the EUCPM and thereby provide local authorities with more support. 1.

How is the Commission planning to ensure that the outermost regions as well as the overseas countries and territories benefit from the same level of protection against forest fires, floods and earthquakes as countries in Europe do?

Could it extend the reach of the EUCPM and the rescEU air fleet beyond a single continent by creating civil protection air bases in the West Indies, the Indian Ocean and the Pacific Ocean that would also work in conjunction with global initiatives tackling the problem of forest fires, so as to bring in international expertise on this subject?
answer: Outermost regions are parts of the EU with the primary responsibility for civil protection lying with the concerned Member State. The EU complements national efforts when a Member State is overwhelmed by a disaster.

Due to the outermost regions’ specific vulnerability to extreme weather events, the Commission has committed itself (1) notably to supporting actions on risk prevention and resilience as regards natural disasters. These regions benefit from a preferential treatment under the EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF) (2), with a threshold for activation set at 1% of regional gross domestic product (instead of the 1.
5% for other regions). The EUSF operates in complementarity with other EU policy instruments that support long term development such as the Cohesion policy funds.

Member States and third countries, including overseas countries and territories, may request assistance through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism (UCPM) (3) to protect people as well as the environment and property against all kinds of natural and man-made disasters. Financing under the UCPM, including as part of rescEU, does not cover civil protection infrastructure, such as air bases.

When developing rescEU assets, the Commission, mindful of the limited resources, applies a sense of proportionality in geographical distribution when deciding where to allocate these assets. Additionally, the Emergency Response Coordination Centre (ERCC) does not preclude the deployment of rescEU assets in outermost regions.

Before deciding on the deployment, the ERCC must consider the appropriateness and adequacy of these assets to respond to the disaster, including their geographic locations, to ensure operational effectiveness.

Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions — Putting people first, securing sustainable and inclusive growth, unlocking the potential of the EU’s outermost regions. https://eurlex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?
